FRIENDLY NEIGHBORHOOD SPIDER-MAN Season 2 Teaser Reveals Symbiote Spider-Man and Ghost-Spider
results.description: Disney revealed the first teaser for Your Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man Season 2 at D23, and Peter’s next adventure is getting much bigger. The footage brings Eddie Brock into the story, gives fans a glimpse of Ghost-Spider, brings back Doctor Octopus and Daredevil, and closes with the symbiote wrapping itself around Peter. Season 1 established this alternate corner of the Spider-Man universe with Peter Parker, Harry Osborn, Nico Minoru, and Lonnie Lincoln, who eventually began his transformation into Tombstone. Season 2 is going to expand that world with more familiar Marvel characters while continuing to put its own spin on Spider-Man mythology. The D23 footage opens at an event attended by Harry Osborn, where Daily Bugle reporter Eddie Brock approaches him looking for an interview. Eddie doesn’t get very far before he’s sent away, but his appearance is obviously worth paying attention to considering what happens later in the teaser. Things get dangerous when Doctor Octopus arrives and grabs Harry as part of his attempt to get revenge on Norman Osborn. Spider-Man jumps into action, battles Doc Ock, and manages to rescue his friend. From there, the footage transitions into the animated series’ intro, which offers quick looks at several villains along with the arrival of Ghost-Spider. Daredevil also appears, with Charlie Cox returning to voice the Man Without Fear. Then comes the big reveal. The symbiote begins consuming Peter, covering his body and transforming him into the black-suited Spider-Man, seemingly setting the stage for Venom to become a major part of Season 2. That development has roots going all the way back to the first season. During the Oscorp incident, a portal to another Earth opened and allowed a symbiote to cross over. Spider-Man teamed up with Doctor Strange to deal with the immediate threat, but clearly that alien goo wasn’t finished causing trouble. Marvel Television and Marvel Animation executive Brad Winderbaum has already confirmed that the symbiotes will be a “significant factor” in Season 2, and the teaser certainly supports that. Eddie Brock showing up at the same time Peter bonds with the symbiote makes it pretty easy to see where the story could be headed. Marvel hasn’t officially confirmed that Eddie will become Venom, but all the necessary pieces are sitting on the board. It would be pretty surprising if the season ended without Eddie getting his own nasty encounter with the alien symbiote. Ghost-Spider is the bigger mystery. The character has previously been confirmed as Gwen Stacy, but we still don’t know exactly how this version of Gwen becomes Ghost-Spider or what her relationship with Peter will look like. Season 1 already established that the multiverse exists when a Doctor Strange from another Earth crossed paths with Peter. However, that doesn’t necessarily mean Ghost-Spider will be another multiversal visitor. This universe has already made major changes to familiar Marvel characters, including its very different interpretation of Nico Minoru, so Gwen could easily receive a new origin created specifically for the series. That possibility is part of what makes Your Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man fun. It uses recognizable characters and pieces of Spider-Man history without being locked into recreating the stories fans already know. Season 1 spent plenty of time developing Peter and Harry’s friendship while also chronicling Lonnie Lincoln’s tragic slide toward becoming Tombstone. Season 2 now has the opportunity to push Peter into much darker territory through the symbiote while adding Eddie Brock and Gwen Stacy to an increasingly crowded mix. And if Peter really does lose himself to the symbiote before Venom enters the picture, things could get rough for everyone around him. Your Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man Season 2 premieres on Disney+ in January 2027.

results.title: New twist in Kawhi Leonard investigation sounds like good news for Toronto Raptors
results.description: It appears Kawhi Leonard might soon finally rejoin the Toronto Raptors. On Monday, ESPN’s Baxter Holmes reported that the NBA’s investigation found no evidence that LA Clippers owner Steve Ballmer funnelled money through team sponsors to pay Leonard as part of a salary-cap circumvention scheme. The investigation stemmed from a September 2025 report from ESPN’s Pablo Torre, which alleged that Aspiration, a now-bankrupt green banking company Ballmer invested in, provided the two-time NBA Finals MVP with a $28 million “no-show” endorsement deal off the books. The new report indicates the NBA has allegedly ruled out that part of the investigation. > NEWS with @DVNJr, @ramonashelburne and @ShamsCharania: The NBA has found no evidence showing LA Clippers owner Steve Ballmer funneled money through team sponsors to pay Kawhi Leonard in order to circumvent the salary cap, sources tell ESPN. https://t.co/zmuTzWdAPd > > — Baxter Holmes (@Baxter) August 17, 2026 The NBA issued a statement in response to the ESPN article, stating that the reporting contained “numerous and significant inaccuracies,” and that the outcome of the investigation will be made clear upon its conclusion. Either way, the league’s investigation into Leonard and the Clippers isn’t over quite yet. According to Holmes, the NBA will continue to investigate whether the Clippers’ introduction of Leonard to team sponsors constitutes a violation of the league’s rules prohibiting salary-cap circumvention. “The league is examining whether the Clippers are guilty of ‘failure to supervise’ employees, though it’s unclear what specific rule the team would have violated or what the penalties would be,” Holmes reported. This investigation has kept Leonard from officially rejoining the Raptors. On June 30, Toronto agreed to send Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, two unprotected first-round picks (2031 and 2033), and two second-round picks (2030 and 2033) to the Clippers in exchange for the 35-year-old small forward. Nearly 10 days later, the Raptors asked the league to pause the trade while the NBA completed its investigation. Leonard and the Raptors are both operating as though the trade will be completed and he’ll land in Toronto, Holmes reported. It is unlikely that Leonard will be announced as a Raptor until the investigation is complete, though Monday’s report is certainly good news for Toronto fans.

results.title: Canada announces $50 billion plan to boost clean energy
results.description: MONTREAL — Canadian officials announced plans Monday to massively enhance wind and hydropower generation in the eastern part of the country, in a project Ottawa called "the largest clean energy investment in North American history." The tentative agreement between Prime Minister Mark Carney's government, the province of Quebec as well as Newfoundland and Labrador marks a major effort to increase electricity production. It includes plans to upgrade the Churchill Falls generating station while developing a new hydro project on Gull Island. Both sites are in Labrador, on Canada's Atlantic coast. Some of the new power generated would also be transmitted to Quebec, with utility Hydro-Quebec selling a significant amount of electricity into the northeastern United States. Carney's office put the total investments in the project at nearly CAN$70 billion ($50.5 billion). But the initiative could be stalled within months. At Monday's signing ceremony in Newfoundland, Quebec Premier Christine Frechette acknowledged that her political opponents, the separatist Parti Quebecois, could tear up the agreement if they win provincial elections in October, an outcome current polls suggest is likely. But if the project moves forward, Carney said the amount of power generated would be "enough to light, heat (and) cool the homes in Toronto, Montreal and Vancouver combined." Since taking office last year, Carney has been criticized by environmentally conscious groups who accuse him of betraying climate pledges backed by his predecessor Justin Trudeau. A member of Carney's cabinet resigned last year over plans to advance a new oil pipeline running from Alberta to the Pacific coast. Monday's announcement was however welcomed by the Canadian Climate Institute, which said it showed "the level of ambition needed to reach Canada's goal of doubling the electricity grid with clean energy." The group's president, Rick Smith, said that enhancing domestic clean energy supply will also "improve energy security and affordability in a time of volatile energy price swings."
